content.introduction: The U.S. corporate profit engine is driving the stock market's rally to record highs, with the S&P 500 up 6% for the year and surging more than 14% since March 30. The U.S. is experiencing a great profit boom, with corporate profits reaching a record $4.7 trillion by mid-year, a 17% increase on the previous year’s figures, largely driven by tax breaks and investments in AI companies. Analysts' estimates for future 12-month U.S. earnings have risen by over 10% since the start of the year. body:
NEW YORK, May 6 (Reuters) - A humming U.S. corporate profit engine is at the heart of the U.S. stock market's rally to record highs - an encouraging sign for investors as long as the fuel driving profits keeps flowing. [...] "Because things have not gotten worse and the ceasefire has been in place for some time now, it's been earnings that have driven the ​move higher," said Chris Fasciano, chief market strategist at Commonwealth Financial Network.

The benchmark S&P 500 (.SPX) is up 6% for the year, building on three straight years of solid double-digit percentage gains. The ​index has surged more than 14% since March 30, following a swoon sparked by the start of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. [...] More than two-thirds through ​the first-quarter reporting season, S&P 500 companies are on track for their highest quarterly earnings growth in more than four years. Future projections are also growing rosier: Analysts' estimates ‌for future 12-month U.S. earnings have risen by over 10% since the start of the year, according to LSEG Datastream.

Sign up here.

The United States is in the throes of a great profit boom. Corporate profits had reached a record $4.7 trillion for the last twelve months by ​mid-year. That’s a 17% increase on the previous year’s figures. Tax breaks contained in President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act have led to a sharp drop in corporate tax receipts. Washington’s enormous ‌fiscal deficit – running at around 6% of GDP – provides an economy wide fillip to corporate bottom lines.

Sign up here. [...] Sign up here.

When it comes to individual companies, however, the surge is all about AI. Earnings per share for members of the S&P 500 Index (.SPX) were up 26% in the twelve months to July: the long-run average annual growth rate is 7%. Expected earnings for the third quarter are 35% above estimates from a year ago. [...] Investments in unlisted AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic ​are also super-charging profits.
